newsitem.title: GERMANY: German newspaper details Leo Kirch sales figures. [CORRECTED 19:43 GMT]
newsitem.headline: German newspaper details Leo Kirch sales figures. [CORRECTED 19:43 GMT]

text.p: The veil of secrecy over the business of German media mogul Leo Kirch was lifted slightly on Wednesday when a German newspaper published what it said were sales figures from the reclusive magnate.

In a report to appear on Thursday, the Munich-based Sueddeutsche Zeitung newspaper said Kirch documents show he tripled his turnover between 1993 and 1995 and put the value of his vast film library at 1.3 billion (corrects from 1.8 billion) marks.
While presenting no information about the profitability of the group, the report said Kirch sales were 455 million marks in 1993, one billion marks in 1994 and 1.43 billion marks in 1995.

With the launch four months ago of his DF1 digital pay television channel, Kirch set off on an investment offensive to boost programming that will peak in 1997 at 1.175 billion marks after 885 billion marks this year.

The programme investment is broken up into ongoing expenditure -- 570 million marks this year and 695 million next year -- and programme acquisitions -- 315 million marks this year and 480 million in 1997.
Programme investment will fall to 850 million marks in 1998 and will be made up of 330 million marks for running costs and 520 million marks in programme acquisitions.

The huge acquisition costs account for Kirch's shopping spree earlier this year when he bought the digital pay TV rights for the films of most Hollywood majors and a rights package for World Cup soccer broadcasts in 2002 and 2006.

Separately, the Hamburg-based pay TV broadcaster Premiere said it has won an injunction against Kirch's DF1 that could affect the way DF1 links its subscription price to leasing charges for its digital TV decoders.
Premiere said DF1's 48-mark monthly package of movies and decoder violated the rights of retailers to offer flexible pricing.
Neither the Kirch Group nor the Hamburg court were available for comment.
